slides.statement:
Google says it may take
*up to* two weeks.
slides.detail: It began on 10 November and applies worldwide, in every language. So UK search results are part of it.

slides.text: In general, most sites don't need to worry about core updates and may not even realize one has happened.
slides.sub: Google Search Central, on core updates
slides.source: developers.google.com, Google Search's core updates and your website.

slides.title: What Google says to do
steps: Google's Search Status Dashboard shows the start and end dates.
Google recommends at least a full week after it completes before analysing anything.
Compare two weeks in Search Console
A week after it finished against a week before it started.
Look at your top pages and searches
Have they slipped a little or a lot?

slides.title:
Then judge the
size of the drop
items: Google: no need for drastic action. Leave pages that are doing well alone.
Google: do a deeper assessment of your whole site and the pages hit hardest.
Deleting content is a last resort, Google says.
slides.source: Examples are Google's own, from its core updates guidance.
